summary: The @gyomu/ts-analysis package provides a robust framework for performing static analysis on TypeScript projects. It enables developers to orchestrate the exploration of workspace projects, process source files into structured metadata, and manage the persistence of analysis results.
responsibilities: Orchestrate the static analysis pipeline from project initialization to file-level processing.
Manage the discovery and structural definition of TypeScript projects within a workspace.
Provide a consistent interface for resolving and transforming file system paths relative to project and workspace roots.
Persist analysis metadata to the filesystem to support incremental processing and efficient lookups.
Bridge the gap between logical module specifiers and physical source code locations.

capabilities.name: Project Discovery
capabilities.description: Enables the identification and structural mapping of TypeScript projects and workspace environments.

capabilities.name: Static Analysis Engine
capabilities.description: Provides core facilities to analyze TypeScript source files and extract symbols and dependency information.

capabilities.name: Persistence Management
capabilities.description: Handles caching and storage of analysis results to disk for improved performance in subsequent operations.

capabilities.name: Path Resolution Framework
capabilities.description: Offers utilities for normalizing, mapping, and translating paths between source files, output artifacts, and module specifiers.

designDecisions: Adopts a context-driven architecture, using 'ProjectContext' and 'WorkspaceContext' to anchor all operations in a defined environment.
Separates core analysis logic from infrastructural concerns like path normalization and workspace discovery.
Utilizes a persistent-first approach for analysis results to ensure scalability and reusability of processed data.
Leverages external static analysis tools, abstracting them into a unified project-wide orchestration layer.
usageGuidance: Always initialize a project or workspace context before executing file-level analysis to ensure correct scope resolution.
Use the provided path utility functions when dealing with file paths to maintain consistency across OS and build environments.
Utilize the built-in persistence methods to cache file analysis results rather than re-analyzing files unnecessarily.
Leverage the testing fixtures provided in the './testing' export path for verifying custom analysis logic.
